newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Queensland okays zinc plant study.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Queensland okays zinc plant study.

text.p: The Queensland government said on Monday it had approved the completion of an impact assessment study for a proposed A$530 million zinc refinery at the port city of Townsville.
Economic Development and Trade Minister Dough Slack said in a statement completion of the study was an important development for the project's owner, the Korea Zinc Co.
"Today's approval by Cabinet brings the construction of the refinery and the creation of new jobs for North Queenslanders a significant step closer," Slack said.
Initially, the refinery is earmarked to produce about 170,000 tonnes of zinc starting in 1999, although Korea Zinc has said a stage two expansion would double output five years later.

The project still needs to meet state environmental license requirements and would be subject to a federal environmental assessment under Australia's Foreign Investment Review Board (FIRB) regulations, Slack said.
The federal government earlier this year said it would help Korea Zinc win FIRB approval.

The federal government at the time also committed help the company achieve environmental approvals, immigration clearance, customs and tariff approvals and access to the Industrial Supplies Office to ensure maximum use of Australian materials in the smelter.
Stage one of the project will create 590 jobs during construction and 350 jobs when in operation, Slack said.
Nationally, the refinery should generate about 2,000 jobs, he said.
